title: Capacity Simulation Sprint & Autoscale SLA Guardrails Playbook (Quarterly)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Define and execute a quarterly 'Capacity Simulation Sprint' that produces a tested playbook of autoscale guardrails, canary/cutover procedures, and cost safety nets for Dedicated pools. This ticket covers planning, scenario design, experiment execution with the runtime/SRE teams, instrumentation targets, and the final published playbook and dashboards. The playbook should allow on-call and platform teams to validate autoscale behavior, perform controlled rollouts, and rapidly roll back or hedge reservations when unit economics break.

Why: We frequently see unexpected P95 latency spikes and cost-per-token regressions during load bursts and model rollouts. A proactive simulation cadence with clear guardrails reduces production incidents and reduces missed customer SLAs.

Scope:
- Create 6 canonical traffic scenarios (steady growth, sudden spike, multi-tenant noisy neighbor, cache cold start, long-seq bursts, degradation & fallthrough).
- Run scenario experiments against a staging Dedicated pool with representative models and quantization profiles.
- Define observable thresholds (latency, error rate, cost delta, GPU saturation signals) mapped to automated and manual mitigations.
- Publish a single-runbook PDF + Confluence doc + console dashboard that can be executed by SRE/Platform in an on-call window.

Out of scope: billing contract changes, long-term reservation pricing strategy (covered in separate capacity economics initiatives).
acceptance_criteria: Six scenarios defined with traffic templates and expected telemetry envelopes
End-to-end experiment runs completed for at least 4 of 6 scenarios in staging Dedicated pool
Dashboard tile that compares baseline vs experiment for P50/P95 latency, errs/min, GPU_util, and cost/hour
Automated rollback trigger defined and validated: when P95 > 600ms AND GPU_util > 92% for 2 consecutive minutes, resize or route to fallback model
Runbook published in Confluence and linked from Console's runbooks section
Postmortem/lessons doc with 3 actionable platform changes (e.g., batching tuning, KV cache warm strategies, kernel selection hints)
tasks: PM: finalize scenario list and success criteria (Aisha)
Eng: implement traffic templates and scenario runners (ENG team lead)
SRE: provision staging Dedicated pool and monitoring hooks (SRE oncall)
Data/Observability: create dashboard and experiment comparison views (Observability team)
Design: produce a one-page runbook UX for Console embedding (Design)
QA: run chaos injection for one scenario (QA)
Publish: Confluence runbook + share in weekly platform sync (PM)
Follow-up: create up to 3 eng tickets for platform changes found in postmortem
metrics: KR1: Reduce production P95 incidents tied to autoscale by 35% quarter-over-quarter
KR2: Decrease median cost-per-1M tokens for dedicated pools under burst by 8% from baseline
KR3: Achieve successful automated rollback validation in staging in >=2 scenarios
KR4: Runbook execution time (time from alert to mitigation) <= 10 minutes in tabletop exercises
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Planning, week 0-2): define scenarios, owners, and instrumentation. Phase 1 (Experiment build, week 3-5): deliver traffic runners and monitoring dashboards. Phase 2 (Staging runs, week 6-8): execute scenarios, iterate on mitigation thresholds. Phase 3 (Dry run & tabletop, week 9): conduct 2 on-call tabletop exercises and finalize playbook. Phase 4 (Publish & training, week 10): publish runbook, embed links in Console, and run a 60-minute training for SRE and platform engineers.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Staging pool not representative of production. Mitigation: mirror model mix and quantization profiles; capture GPU telemetry at same granularity.
Risk: Experiment runs cause noisy neighbor effects that impact other teams. Mitigation: schedule low-impact windows and notify stakeholders; use isolated tenancy when possible.
Risk: False positives from telemetry thresholds. Mitigation: validate thresholds across historical traces and multi-run statistical checks before enabling automated actions.
